1	# Vortex GPGPU
2	
3	Vortex is a full-stack open-source RISC-V GPGPU. Vortex supports multiple **backend drivers**, including our C++ simulator (simx), an RTL simulator, and physical Xilinx and Altera FPGAs-- all controlled by a single driver script. The chosen driver determines the corresponding code invoked to run Vortex. Generally, developers will prototype their intended design in simx, before completing going forward with an RTL implementation. Alternatively, you can get up and running by selecting a driver of your choice and running a demo program.
4	
5	## Website
6	Vortex news can be found on its [website](https://vortex.cc.gatech.edu/)
7	
8	## Citation
9	```
10	@inproceedings{10.1145/3466752.3480128,
11		author = {Tine, Blaise and Yalamarthy, Krishna Praveen and Elsabbagh, Fares and Hyesoon, Kim},
12		title = {Vortex: Extending the RISC-V ISA for GPGPU and 3D-Graphics},
13		year = {2021},
14		isbn = {9781450385572},
15		publisher = {Association for Computing Machinery},
16		address = {New York, NY, USA},
17		url = {https://doi.org/10.1145/3466752.3480128},
18		doi = {10.1145/3466752.3480128},
19		abstract = {The importance of open-source hardware and software has been increasing. However, despite GPUs being one of the more popular accelerators across various applications, there is very little open-source GPU infrastructure in the public domain. We argue that one of the reasons for the lack of open-source infrastructure for GPUs is rooted in the complexity of their ISA and software stacks. In this work, we first propose an ISA extension to RISC-V that supports GPGPUs and graphics. The main goal of the ISA extension proposal is to minimize the ISA changes so that the corresponding changes to the open-source ecosystem are also minimal, which makes for a sustainable development ecosystem. To demonstrate the feasibility of the minimally extended RISC-V ISA, we implemented the complete software and hardware stacks of Vortex on FPGA. Vortex is a PCIe-based soft GPU that supports OpenCL and OpenGL. Vortex can be used in a variety of applications, including machine learning, graph analytics, and graphics rendering. Vortex can scale up to 32 cores on an Altera Stratix 10 FPGA, delivering a peak performance of 25.6 GFlops at 200 Mhz.},
20		booktitle = {MICRO-54: 54th Annual IEEE/ACM International Symposium on Microarchitecture},
21		pages = {754–766},
22		numpages = {13},
23		keywords = {reconfigurable computing, memory systems., computer graphics},
24		location = {Virtual Event, Greece},
25		series = {MICRO '21}
26	}
27	```
28	
29	## Specifications
30	
31	- Support RISC-V RV32IMAFC and RV64IMAFDC
32	
33	- Microarchitecture:
34	    - configurable number of cores, warps, and threads.
35	    - configurable number of ALU, FPU, LSU, and SFU units per core.
36	    - graphics fixed-function pipeline (rasterizer, texture units, output mergers).
37	    - hardware ray-tracing unit (BVH traversal, ray-box and ray-triangle intersection).
38	    - tensor cores with WGMMA and 2:4 structured sparsity support.
39	    - hardware-accelerated command processor and kernel management unit.
40	    - configurable pipeline issue width.
41	    - optional local memory, L1, L2, and L3 caches.
42	- Software:
43	    - OpenCL 1.2
44	    - Vulkan
45	    - HIP
46	- Supported FPGAs:
47	    - Altera Arria 10
48	    - Altera Stratix 10
49	    - Xilinx Alveo U50, U55C, U250, U280
50	    - Xilinx Versal VCK5000
51	
52	## Directory structure
53	
54	- `doc`: [Documentation](docs/index.md).
55	- `hw`: Hardware sources.
56	- `sw`: Software sources (kernel, runtime, and drivers).
57	- `sim`: Simulators repository.
58	- `tests`: Tests repository.
59	- `ci`: Continuous integration scripts.
60	- `miscs`: Miscellaneous resources.
61	- `VX_config.toml` / `VX_types.toml`: Hardware configuration system.
62	
63	## Quick Start
64	If you are interested in a stable release of Vortex, you can download the latest release [here](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/releases/latest). Otherwise, you can pull the most recent, but (potentially) unstable version as shown below. The following steps demonstrate how to build and run Vortex with the default driver: SimX. If you are interested in a different backend, look [here](docs/simulation.md).
65	
66	### Supported OS Platforms
67	- Ubuntu 22.04
68	- Centos 7
69	### Toolchain Dependencies
70	The following dependencies will be fetched prebuilt by `toolchain_install.sh`.
71	- [POCL](http://portablecl.org/)
72	- [LLVM](https://llvm.org/)
73	- [RISCV-GNU-TOOLCHAIN](https://github.com/riscv-collab/riscv-gnu-toolchain)
74	- [Verilator](https://www.veripool.org/verilator)
75	- [cvfpu](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu.git)
76	- [SoftFloat](https://github.com/ucb-bar/berkeley-softfloat-3.git)
77	- [Ramulator](https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/ramulator.git)
78	- [Yosys](https://github.com/YosysHQ/yosys)
79	- [Sv2v](https://github.com/zachjs/sv2v)
80	- [Mesa](https://www.mesa3d.org/)
81	- [chipStar](https://github.com/CHIP-Star/chipStar)
82	### Install Vortex codebase
83	```sh
84		git clone --depth=1 --recursive https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex.git
85		cd vortex
86	```
87	### Install system dependencies
88	```sh
89	# ensure dependent libraries are present
90	sudo ./ci/install_dependencies.sh
91	```
92	### Configure your build folder
93	```sh
94	    mkdir build
95	    cd build
96	    # for 32bit
97	    ../configure --xlen=32 --tooldir=$HOME/tools
98	    # for 64bit
99	    ../configure --xlen=64 --tooldir=$HOME/tools
100	```
101	### Install prebuilt toolchain
102	```sh
103	   ./ci/toolchain_install.sh
104	```
105	
106	### Building and installing Vortex
107	```sh
108	make -s
109	make install
110	export VORTEX_PATH=$(pwd)/install
111	export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=$VORTEX_PATH/lib/pkgconfig:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH
112	```
113	`make install` lays out a sysroot under `$VORTEX_PATH` containing the
114	public headers, libraries, and `vortex-runtime.pc` / `vortex-kernel.pc`
115	pkg-config files. Downstream tools (mesa-vortex, pocl-vortex,
116	chipstar) integrate with Vortex exclusively through `$VORTEX_PATH` and
117	pkg-config — the same shape as the CUDA, ROCm and oneAPI SDKs. The
118	source tree (`$VORTEX_HOME`) and build tree (`$VORTEX_BUILD_DIR`) are
119	internal to Vortex and not exposed to consumers. Override the install
120	root with `../configure --prefix=<path>` or `--installdir=<path>` (default `<build>/install`).
121	
122	### Quick demo running vecadd OpenCL kernel on 2 cores
123	```sh
124	./ci/blackbox.sh --cores=2 --app=vecadd
125	```
126	
127	### Compiler Toolchain (VOLT)
128	
129	Vortex's compiler toolchain is **[VOLT](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/Volt)** (Vortex-Optimized Lightweight Toolchain), an LLVM-based SIMT compiler for the Vortex GPU. To build the toolchain locally instead of using the prebuilt one, follow the instructions in the [VOLT repo](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/Volt). Its design is described in the [VOLT paper (CC '26)](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3771775.3786275).
130	
131	### Common Developer Tips
132	- Building Vortex 64-bit requires setting --xlen=64 configure option.
133	```sh
134	../configure --xlen=64 --tooldir=$HOME/tools
135	```
136	- No shell environment setup is required. `../configure` bakes the full
137	  toolchain layout (paths, XCONFIGS, every tool binary) into the build
138	  dir's `config.mk` and domain `common.mk` files. Make recipes invoke
139	  tools by absolute path (`$(VERILATOR_PATH)/bin/verilator` etc.), so
140	  multiple Vortex trees on the same machine can coexist without any
141	  `~/.bashrc` sourcing.
142	- Making changes to Makefiles in your source tree, editing `VX_config.toml` (or any `*.toml`), or adding new folders will require executing the "configure" script again without any options to get changes propagated to your build folder.
143	```sh
144	../configure
145	```
146	- Always make sure your build is up to date before running any test or app: re-run `../configure` from your build folder first. `configure` regenerates `<build>/sw/VX_config.h` and `<build>/hw/*.vh` from `VX_config.toml` (only when the toml is newer). The simulator and RTL `#include` this generated header, so a stale header makes them compile against old config values and silently diverge from the toml. `VX_config.toml` is the single source of truth — never paper over a divergence by hardcoding `-DVX_CFG_*` flags in a Makefile; re-`configure` instead.
147	- To debug the GPU, the simulation can generate a runtime trace for analysis. See /docs/debugging.md for more information.
148	```sh
149	./ci/blackbox.sh --app=demo --debug=3
150	```
151	- Running the CI suite locally: the test catalog lives in `ci/testcases/` and runs
152	  through pytest via the `regression.sh` wrapper (from your build folder). See
153	  [docs/continuous_integration.md](docs/continuous_integration.md) for details.
154	```sh
155	./ci/regression.sh --all               # full catalog
156	./ci/regression.sh --test regression   # one category
157	```
158	- For additional information, check out the [documentation](docs/index.md)
159

- `sim`: Simulators repository.
- `tests`: Tests repository.
- `ci`: Continuous integration scripts.

- Ubuntu 22.04
- Centos 7

- [LLVM](https://llvm.org/)
- [RISCV-GNU-TOOLCHAIN](https://github.com/riscv-collab/riscv-gnu-toolchain)
- [Verilator](https://www.veripool.org/verilator)
- [cvfpu](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cvfpu.git)
- [SoftFloat](https://github.com/ucb-bar/berkeley-softfloat-3.git)
- [Ramulator](https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/ramulator.git)
- [Yosys](https://github.com/YosysHQ/yosys)
- [Sv2v](https://github.com/zachjs/sv2v)
- [Mesa](https://www.mesa3d.org/)
- [chipStar](https://github.com/CHIP-Star/chipStar)

```sh

### Install system dependencies
```sh

sudo ./ci/install_dependencies.sh
```
### Configure your build folder
```sh
    mkdir build
    cd build
    # for 32bit
    ../configure --xlen=32 --tooldir=$HOME/tools
    # for 64bit
    ../configure --xlen=64 --tooldir=$HOME/tools
```
### Install prebuilt toolchain
```sh
   ./ci/toolchain_install.sh
```

```sh
make -s
make install

export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=$VORTEX_PATH/lib/pkgconfig:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH
```
`make install` lays out a sysroot under `$VORTEX_PATH` containing the
public headers, libraries, and `vortex-runtime.pc` / `vortex-kernel.pc`
pkg-config files. Downstream tools (mesa-vortex, pocl-vortex,
chipstar) integrate with Vortex exclusively through `$VORTEX_PATH` and

source tree (`$VORTEX_HOME`) and build tree (`$VORTEX_BUILD_DIR`) are
internal to Vortex and not exposed to consumers. Override the install
root with `../configure --prefix=<path>` or `--installdir=<path>` (default `<build>/install`).

### Quick demo running vecadd OpenCL kernel on 2 cores
```sh
./ci/blackbox.sh --cores=2 --app=vecadd
```

### Compiler Toolchain (VOLT)

Vortex's compiler toolchain is **[VOLT](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/Volt)** (Vortex-Optimized Lightweight Toolchain), an LLVM-based SIMT compiler for the Vortex GPU. To build the toolchain locally instead of using the prebuilt one, follow the instructions in the [VOLT repo](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/Volt). ### Common Developer Tips
- Building Vortex 64-bit requires setting --xlen=64 configure option.
```sh
../configure --xlen=64 --tooldir=$HOME/tools
```
- No shell environment setup is required. `../configure` bakes the full
  toolchain layout (paths, XCONFIGS, every tool binary) into the build
  dir's `config.mk` and domain `common.mk` files. Make recipes invoke
  tools by absolute path (`$(VERILATOR_PATH)/bin/verilator` etc.), so
  multiple Vortex trees on the same machine can coexist without any
  `~/.bashrc` sourcing.
- Making changes to Makefiles in your source tree, editing `VX_config.toml` (or any `*.toml`), or adding new folders will require executing the "configure" script again without any options to get changes propagated to your build folder.
```sh
../configure
```
- Always make sure your build is up to date before running any test or app: re-run `../configure` from your build folder first. `configure` regenerates `<build>/sw/VX_config.h` and `<build>/hw/*.vh` from `VX_config.toml` (only when the toml is newer). - To debug the GPU, the simulation can generate a runtime trace for analysis. See /docs/debugging.md for more information.
```sh
./ci/blackbox.sh --app=demo --debug=3
```
- Running the CI suite locally: the test catalog lives in `ci/testcases/` and runs
  through pytest via the `regression.sh` wrapper (from your build folder). See
  [docs/continuous_integration.md](docs/continuous_integration.md) for details.
```sh
./ci/regression.sh --all               # full catalog
./ci/regression.sh --test regression   # one category
```
- For additional information, check out the [documentation](docs/index.md)

159

169	- **Branch-specific addenda are forbidden.** Branch context goes in a `docs/proposals/<feature>_proposal.md`, not in branch-local `AGENTS.md` variants. If the rule is general, promote it here; if it's a project-tracking detail, keep it in the proposal.

- **`--rebuild=1` forces a driver rebuild** even if the hardware configuration is unchanged. Use it when iterating on the driver itself; `--rebuild=0` suppresses rebuild regardless.
- **Keep smoke/regression runs lean.** Don't enable debug or perf collection unless the run is explicitly for debug or measurement.
- **RTL coverage path is `xrt`, not `rtlsim`.** When discussing or planning RTL verification, `xrt` is the canonical path — `rtlsim` bypasses the AFU surface. `rtlsim` remains useful for fast iteration on processor RTL; `xrt` is what proves the full integration.
- **`ci/regression.sh` is the canonical source of tested configurations.** Use it to discover supported parameter combinations before inventing ad hoc ones.
- **Perf-regression baselines (`ci/perf/baselines/*.json`) are golden data — never hand-edit them, and never "fix" a red perf gate by bumping the number.** They are regenerated only by `pytest ci -m perf_gate --update-baselines` (a human-run, reviewed step), and CI must never pass that flag. A `perf_gate` failure means real cycles moved: root-cause it, or — if the change is intended — regenerate the baseline so the diff shows the perf delta for review. Same rule as image goldens and `known_issue:`.
- **SimX is the RTL's timing model — keep them in lockstep.** Any change that moves RTL cycles (pipeline structure, arbitration, queue depths, cache/memory behavior) must land together with the matching SimX timing-model update, and vice-versa. The `model_parity` CI gate enforces this: a `check: model_parity` case (`ci/testcases/model_parity.yaml` + per-extension parity categories) runs the same app/args/configs on simx and rtlsim and asserts exact retired-instruction match plus cycle agreement within the case tolerance (default 5%). Never widen a tolerance to absorb a divergence — model the behavior. When adding a hardware feature, add or extend a parity case that exercises it.
- **When RTL debugging stalls, switch to the SimX-as-oracle pattern.** For numerical bugs, deep pipeline races, or any failure mode where rtlsim is "close but wrong": (1) build/extend the SimX C++ model so it mirrors the *new* RTL architecture and gets to PASS; (2) add matching trace dumps to both SimX and RTL (cycle, FU events, SRAM addresses+data, hazards) — same CSV format on both sides; (3) diff trace files — the first divergence is the bug. Don't keep guessing from output values; localize via trace diff. See [docs/debugging.md](docs/debugging.md#simx-as-oracle-for-rtl-debug).

```bash
./ci/blackbox.sh --driver=simx --app=demo
./ci/blackbox.sh --driver=simx --app=sgemm --args="-n10"
```

### Regression suites

```bash
make -C tests/regression run-simx
make -C tests/regression run-rtlsim
make -C tests/opencl     run-simx
make -C tests/opencl     run-rtlsim
```

### Architecture overrides

`blackbox.sh` exposes the common knobs directly: `--clusters=`, `--cores=`, `--warps=`, `--threads=`, `--l2cache`, `--l3cache`, `--debug=`, `--perf=`. For anything not exposed as a flag, use `CONFIGS="-D..."` (all parameters take the `VX_CFG_*` prefix — e.g. `-DVX_CFG_NUM_THREADS=8`, `-DVX_CFG_EXT_TCU_ENABLE`). Baseline parameters live in `VX_config.toml` and `VX_types.toml` at the repo root — edit those only when an override is needed for *all* builds, and re-`configure` afterward.

```bash
./ci/blackbox.sh --driver=simx --app=sgemm --clusters=1 --cores=2 --warps=4 --threads=4 --l2cache
```
OR

```bash
CONFIGS="-DVX_CFG_NUM_THREADS=4 -DVX_CFG_EXT_TCU_ENABLE -DVX_CFG_TCU_TYPE_TFR -DITYPE=bf16 -DOTYPE=fp32" ./ci/blackbox.sh --driver=rtlsim --app=sgemm_tcu
```

### Roofline Analysis

Use `--perf=1` for detailed performance counters such as scheduler utilization, pipeline stalls, instruction mix, and memory latency.

```bash
/usr/bin/python3 ../perf/roofline.py --app=sgemm_tcu --driver=simx --cores=1 --warps=4 --threads=8 --issue-width=2 --perf=1 --by-cycle --output=sgemm_tcu_roofline.png
```

---

## 5. Design & Architecture Rules

- **Align with mainstream CUDA, HIP, OpenCL, and Vulkan API and driver stacks.** For any design question — driver surface, command-processor model, memory model, scheduling — pick the solution those stacks would use. This keeps Vortex's externals familiar to mainstream software and avoids one-off abstractions.

- **SimX Cardinal Rule — modules communicate *only* through channels.** A `SimObject` may observe or mutate another module's state *only* via its bound `SimChannel` ports (`MemReq`/`MemRsp`, `result_if`, …). **Never reach across the ownership hierarchy** to touch another object directly (`core_->processor()->memsim()`, `parent()->child()->field`, a leaf unit grabbing the global `Memory`). See [docs/simobject.md](docs/simobject.md#the-cardinal-rule).

---

## 6. Coding Conventions

See [docs/coding_guidelines_cpp.md](docs/coding_guidelines_cpp.md) and [docs/coding_guidelines_verilog.md](docs/coding_guidelines_verilog.md) for full style. Cross-cutting comment rules:

- **`sw/{kernel,runtime}/` and `sim/`/`hw/` are bidirectionally isolated.** Source files under `sw/kernel/` and `sw/runtime/` MUST NOT reference anything in `hw/*` or `sim/*`. Equally, source files under `sim/*` and `hw/*` MUST NOT reference anything in `sw/kernel/` or `sw/runtime/`. If the layers genuinely need to share host-side helper code or an on-wire ABI definition, put it in `sw/common/` — vortex-internal, never installed, accessible from all four layers. Enforced by [ci/check_sw_sim_boundary.sh](ci/check_sw_sim_boundary.sh).
- **Default to no comment.** Add one only when the *why* is non-obvious — a hidden constraint, a subtle invariant, a workaround for a specific bug, a surprising behavior.
- **Comments explain *why*, not *what*.** Well-named identifiers carry the *what*.
- **Never reference the current task, PR, caller, issue number, or fix.** Those belong in the commit message and rot in code. Don't write `// used by foo()`, `// added for the X flow`, `// handles issue #123`.
- **`RTL_PKGS` is for `VX_*_pkg.sv` only.** Verilog interfaces are illegal there. If an interface isn't being discovered, fix it via include paths or file naming — not by stuffing it into `RTL_PKGS`.
- **Library RTL defaults to `TRACING_OFF`.** Modules under `hw/rtl/libs/` are excluded from VCD by default to keep waveform size manageable. Toggle per-file with `TRACING_ON`/`TRACING_OFF`, or globally with `CONFIGS="-DTRACING_ALL"`.
- **No multi-paragraph docstrings or multi-line block comments** for trivial code. One short line is the ceiling unless the logic genuinely needs more.
- **No `// removed code` or stale-rename breadcrumbs.** If something is unused, delete it.

---

## 7. Proposals

Design and migration proposals belong in [`docs/proposals/`](docs/proposals/) — never in build dirs or the repo root. A proposal captures the *why* of a non-trivial change before the code lands.

Accepted designs that outlive their proposal phase live in [`docs/designs/`](docs/designs/).

---

## 8. Living Document Policy

This file is versioned alongside the code and evolves with it. Both humans and agents are expected to update it:

- **Add a rule** when you discover a footgun the next contributor will hit. Include the *why*.
- **Update or remove a rule** that's gone stale. A stale rule is worse than no rule.
- **Don't duplicate** content from the topic docs in `docs/`. AGENTS.md links; the topic doc explains.
- **Branch-specific addenda are forbidden.** Branch context goes in a `docs/proposals/<feature>_proposal.md`, not in branch-local `AGENTS.md` variants. If the rule is general, promote it here; if it's a project-tracking detail, keep it in the proposal.

# Vortex Codebase

The directory/file layout of the Vortex codebase is as follows:

- `VX_config.toml` / `VX_types.toml`: hardware configuration system — the single
  source of truth for all build-time parameters (see the
  [build configuration system](designs/build_configuration_system.md)).
- `ci`: continuous integration scripts
  - `testcases`: declarative test catalog (YAML), executed by the pytest harness
  - `perf/baselines`: golden performance baselines for the perf-regression gate
  - `blackbox.sh`: universal application launcher for all drivers
  - `regression.sh`: local entry point into the CI catalog
- `docs`: documentation
  - `designs`: detailed design documents for Vortex subsystems
- `hw`:
  - `rtl`: hardware RTL sources
    - `core`: core pipeline (fetch, decode, issue, execute, LSU, commit)
    - `cache`: cache subsystem (banks, MSHR, AMO engine, flush)
    - `mem`: memory subsystem (arbiters, adapters, local memory)
    - `fpu`: floating point unit
    - `cp`: command processor
    - `tcu`: tensor core unit (WGMMA, structured sparsity)
    - `dxa`: asynchronous data-transfer accelerator (DMA/multicast)
    - `rtu`: ray-tracing unit (BVH traversal, intersection)
    - `raster`, `tex`, `om`, `gfx`: graphics fixed-function pipeline
      (rasterizer, texture units, output merger, shared graphics logic)
    - `afu`: FPGA accelerator functional unit shells (OPAE, XRT)
    - `interfaces`: SystemVerilog interfaces for inter-module communication
    - `libs`: general-purpose RTL modules (queues, arbiters, crossbars, encoders)
  - `dpi`: DPI models shared by the RTL simulators
  - `syn`: synthesis flows
    - `altera`: Altera Quartus synthesis scripts
    - `xilinx`: Xilinx Vivado/Vitis synthesis scripts
    - `synopsys`: Synopsys ASIC synthesis scripts
    - `yosys`: Yosys open-source synthesis scripts
  - `unittest`: Verilator-based unit tests for individual hardware components
  - `scripts`: RTL build and preprocessing utilities
- `sw`: software stack
  - `kernel`: device-side kernel API
    - `include`: public kernel headers (installed)
    - `src`: kernel runtime implementation (startup, scheduling intrinsics)
    - `linker`: linker scripts for kernel binaries
  - `runtime`: host-side runtime and drivers
    - `include`: public driver headers (installed)
    - `stub`: driver stub library (dynamic backend dispatch)
    - `simx`: driver backend for the SimX simulator
    - `rtlsim`: driver backend for the RTL simulator
    - `opae`: Intel OPAE FPGA driver (targets: fpga | asesim | opaesim)
    - `xrt`: Xilinx XRT FPGA driver (targets: hw | hw_emu | sw_emu)
    - `gem5`: driver backend for gem5 full-system integration
  - `common`: vortex-internal shared layer (on-wire ABI structs, host-side
    hardware models, shared helpers) — never installed
  - `gfx`: graphics fixed-function software emitters
- `sim`: simulators
  - `simx`: cycle-approximate C++ simulator
  - `rtlsim`: Verilator-based processor RTL simulator
  - `opaesim`: Intel OPAE AFU RTL simulator
  - `xrtsim`: Xilinx XRT AFU RTL simulator
  - `common`: shared simulator infrastructure (command processor model,
    DRAM model, ELF loader, virtual memory)
- `tests`: test suites
  - `riscv`: RISC-V conformance tests
  - `kernel`: device kernel tests
  - `regression`: host + kernel regression tests
  - `unittest`: host-side unit tests
  - `opencl`: OpenCL benchmarks and tests
  - `vulkan`: Vulkan tests (via the mesa-vortex driver)
  - `hip`: HIP tests (via chipStar)
  - `graphics`: graphics pipeline tests
  - `raytracing`: ray-tracing unit tests
  - `runtime`: driver API tests
  - `mpi`: multi-process tests
- `third_party`: external library submodules (cvfpu, softfloat, hardfloat,
  ramulator, cocogfx)
- `perf`: performance analysis resources
- `miscs`: miscellaneous resources

# Vortex Microarchitecture

### Vortex GPGPU Execution Model

Vortex uses the SIMT (Single Instruction, Multiple Threads) execution model with a single warp issued per cycle.

- **Threads**
  - Smallest unit of computation
  - Each thread has its own register file (32 int + 32 fp registers)
  - Threads execute in parallel
- **Warps**
  - A logical cluster of threads
  - Each thread in a warp execute the same instruction
    - The PC is shared; maintain thread mask for Writeback
  - Warp's execution is time-multiplexed at log steps
    - Ex. warp 0 executes at cycle 0, warp 1 executes at cycle 1

### Vortex RISC-V ISA Extension

- **Thread Mask Control**
  - Control the number of warps to activate during execution
  - `TMC` *count*: activate count threads
- **Warp Scheduling**
  - Control the number of warps to activate during execution
  - `WSPAWN` *count, addr*: activate count warps and jump to addr location
- **Control-Flow Divergence**
  - Control threads activation when a branch diverges
    - `SPLIT` *taken, predicate*: apply predicate thread mask and save current state into IPDOM stack
    - `JOIN`: pop IPDOM stack to restore thread mask
    - `PRED` *predicate, restore_mask*: thread predicate instruction
- **Warp Synchronization**
  - `BAR` *id, count*: stall warps entering barrier *id* until count is reached

### Vortex Pipeline/Datapath

![Image of Vortex Microarchitecture](../assets/img/vortex_microarchitecture.png)

Vortex has a 6-stage pipeline:

- **Schedule**
  - Warp Scheduler
    - Schedule the next PC into the pipeline
    - Track stalled, active warps
  - IPDOM Stack
    - Save split/join states for divergent threads
  - Inflight Tracker
    - Track in-flight instructions

- **Fetch**
  - Retrieve instructions from memory
  - Handle I-cache requests/responses
- **Decode**
  - Decode fetched instructions
  - Notify warp scheduler on control instructions
- **Issue**
  - IBuffer
    - Store decoded instructions in separate per-warp queues
  - Scoreboard
    - Track in-use registers
    - Check register use for decoded instructions
  - Operands Collector
    - Fetch the operands for issued instructions from the register file
- **Execute**
  - ALU Unit
    - Handle arithmetic and branch operations
  - FPU Unit
    - Handle floating-point operations
  - LSU Unit
    - Handle load/store operations
  - SFU Unit
    - Handle warp control operations
    - Handle Control Status Registers (CSRs) operations
  - TCU Unit
    - Handle warp matrix multiply accumulate operations
- **Commit**
  - Write result back to the register file and update the Scoreboard.

### Vortex clustering architecture
- Sockets
  - Grouping multiple cores sharing L1 cache
- Clusters
  - Grouping of sockets sharing L2 cache

### Vortex Cache Subsystem
More details about the cache subsystem are provided [here](cache_subsystem.md).

1	# SimX — Cycle-Approximate Simulator — Design
2	
3	**Scope:** the architecture of SimX, the Vortex cycle-approximate C++
4	simulator ([`sim/simx/`](../../sim/simx/)), and its SST integration
5	([`sim/simx/sst/`](../../sim/simx/sst/)).
6	
7	This document is architectural. The `SimObject`/`SimChannel` framework
8	mechanics are in [`docs/simobject.md`](../simobject.md) and usage is in
9	[`docs/simulation.md`](../simulation.md); this doc covers the v3 model —
10	how functional and timing meet, the module decomposition, and the SST
11	boundary — without repeating those.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. The v3 model: functional + timing in one place
16	
17	The defining property of SimX v3: there is **no central `Emulator`**. ISA
18	semantics live in the same module that models the timing of the
19	corresponding hardware block. ALU and FPU own private `execute()`
20	methods; the SFU routes to its sub-units; CSR/WCTL semantics live in their
21	sub-unit classes; warp/CTA/barrier state lives in `Scheduler`; register
22	files live in `OpcUnit`; decode lives in `Decoder`. Data flows through the
23	memory hierarchy as real payload — caches and DRAM carry line data, and
24	there is no `core->mem_read/mem_write` back door (those names survive only
25	as perf-counter labels).
26	
27	This makes SimX a faithful, module-by-module twin of the RTL, which is why
28	it serves as the RTL oracle for cycle-parity debugging.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## 2. Framework
33	
34	[`sim/common/simobject.h`](../../sim/common/simobject.h) provides:
35	
36	- **`SimObject<Impl>`** (CRTP) — a hardware block with `on_tick`/`on_reset`
37	  hooks; passive objects auto-skip.
38	- **`SimChannel<Pkt>`** — a typed, backpressured link: a producer
39	  `send(pkt, delay)` schedules delivery; `pending_count_` enforces
40	  capacity-based occupancy; `tx_callback` allows snooping. **The channel
41	  is the pipeline** — latency is the `send` delay and occupancy is the
42	  output channel's capacity, so pipelined units need no internal stage
43	  deque.
44	- **`SimPlatform`** — the singleton tick engine: a 4096-bucket timing
45	  wheel plus immediate/delta event queues. Each `tick()` settles delta
46	  events, ticks every active object in creation order, settles deltas
47	  again, advances the cycle, then fires wheel events for that cycle.
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 3. Component inventory
52	
53	**Orchestration**
54	- [`main.cpp`](../../sim/simx/main.cpp) — the standalone `simx` CLI driver.
55	- [`processor.{h,cpp}`](../../sim/simx/processor.cpp) — `Processor`: owns
56	  clusters + the single `Memory` (DRAM), aggregates perf, exposes
57	  `cycle()` (single-cycle step) and `any_running()`.
58	- `cluster.{cpp,h}` → `socket.{cpp,h}` → `core.{cpp,h}` — the GPU
59	  hierarchy; `Core` wires the per-core pipeline.
60	
61	**Per-core pipeline** (mostly `SimObject`s)
62	- `scheduler.{cpp,h}` — per-warp lifecycle: PC/tmask/fcsr/IPDOM stack,
63	  barriers, trap state; owns the `CtaDispatcher` and a `BarrierUnit`.
64	- `cta_dispatcher.{cpp,h}` — CTA → warp (block/grid) mapping.

# SimX — Cycle-Approximate Simulator — Design

**Scope:** the architecture of SimX, the Vortex cycle-approximate C++
simulator ([`sim/simx/`](../../sim/simx/)), and its SST integration
([`sim/simx/sst/`](../../sim/simx/sst/)).

This document is architectural. The `SimObject`/`SimChannel` framework
mechanics are in [`docs/simobject.md`](../simobject.md) and usage is in
[`docs/simulation.md`](../simulation.md); this doc covers the v3 model —
how functional and timing meet, the module decomposition, and the SST
boundary — without repeating those.

---

## 1. The v3 model: functional + timing in one place

The defining property of SimX v3: there is **no central `Emulator`**. ISA
semantics live in the same module that models the timing of the
corresponding hardware block. ALU and FPU own private `execute()`
methods; the SFU routes to its sub-units; CSR/WCTL semantics live in their
sub-unit classes; warp/CTA/barrier state lives in `Scheduler`; register
files live in `OpcUnit`; decode lives in `Decoder`. Data flows through the
memory hierarchy as real payload — caches and DRAM carry line data, and
there is no `core->mem_read/mem_write` back door (those names survive only
as perf-counter labels).

This makes SimX a faithful, module-by-module twin of the RTL, which is why
it serves as the RTL oracle for cycle-parity debugging.

---

## 2. Framework

[`sim/common/simobject.h`](../../sim/common/simobject.h) provides:

- **`SimObject<Impl>`** (CRTP) — a hardware block with `on_tick`/`on_reset`
  hooks; passive objects auto-skip.
- **`SimChannel<Pkt>`** — a typed, backpressured link: a producer
  `send(pkt, delay)` schedules delivery; `pending_count_` enforces
  capacity-based occupancy; `tx_callback` allows snooping. **The channel
  is the pipeline** — latency is the `send` delay and occupancy is the
  output channel's capacity, so pipelined units need no internal stage
  deque.
- **`SimPlatform`** — the singleton tick engine: a 4096-bucket timing
  wheel plus immediate/delta event queues. Each `tick()` settles delta
  events, ticks every active object in creation order, settles deltas
  again, advances the cycle, then fires wheel events for that cycle.

---

## 3. Component inventory

**Orchestration**
- [`main.cpp`](../../sim/simx/main.cpp) — the standalone `simx` CLI driver.
- [`processor.{h,cpp}`](../../sim/simx/processor.cpp) — `Processor`: owns
  clusters + the single `Memory` (DRAM), aggregates perf, exposes
  `cycle()` (single-cycle step) and `any_running()`.
- `cluster.{cpp,h}` → `socket.{cpp,h}` → `core.{cpp,h}` — the GPU
  hierarchy; `Core` wires the per-core pipeline.

**Per-core pipeline** (mostly `SimObject`s)
- `scheduler.{cpp,h}` — per-warp lifecycle: PC/tmask/fcsr/IPDOM stack,
  barriers, trap state; owns the `CtaDispatcher` and a `BarrierUnit`.
- `cta_dispatcher.{cpp,h}` — CTA → warp (block/grid) mapping.
- `barrier_unit.{cpp,h}` — barrier arrival/release tracking.
- `sequencer.{cpp,h}` — per-warp micro-op expander (multi-uop TCU
  WMMA/WGMMA; simple instructions pass through).
- `decode.{cpp,h}` — `Decoder`: RISC-V decode into `Instr`.
- `decompressor.{cpp,h}` — RVC fetch decompressor.
- `scoreboard.{cpp,h}` — register hazard tracking / in-order completion.
- `operands.{cpp,h}` + `opc_unit.{cpp,h}` — `Operands` routes to per-lane
  `OpcUnit`s, which own the per-warp register files and do writeback
  (mirrors RTL `VX_opc_unit.sv`).
- `dispatcher.{cpp,h}` — aggregates `ISSUE_WIDTH` issue ports onto per-FU
  execution lanes.
- `func_unit.h` — `FuncUnit<NUM_BLOCKS>` CRTP base; each FU owns
  `Inputs[]`/`Outputs[]` channels.

**Functional units**
- `alu_unit`, `fpu_unit` — own private `execute()` (ISA semantics).
- `lsu_unit` — loads/stores/AMO; `LsuUopGen` for packed loads; pulls load
  data from `MemRsp::data`.
- `sfu_unit` — special-function dispatcher routing to sub-units: WCTL,
  CSR, TEX, RASTER, DXA, OM.
- `csr_unit`, `wctl_unit` — SFU sub-units (CSR/FCSR/MPM; warp control →
  `Scheduler`).
- optional `tcu_unit.*` plus graphics `tex/`, `raster/`, `om/`, `dxa/`.

**Memory** ([`sim/simx/mem/`](../../sim/simx/mem/) + `amo/`)
- `mem_coalescer` — per-LSU-block coalescer.
- `cache.{cpp,h}` — `Cache`: tags + MSHRs + replacement **and line data**;
  embeds the AMO unit.
- `cache_cluster` — shared L2/L3 wrapper.
- `memory.{cpp,h}` — `Memory`: bottom-of-hierarchy DRAM (ramulator2);
  `attach_ram(RAM*)` owns the image; carries data in `MemRsp`; exposes
  `set_pre_send_hook` for SST mirroring.
- `amo/amo_unit.{cpp,h}` — AMO RMW in the cache hierarchy (see
  [`atomic_memory_operations.md`](atomic_memory_operations.md)).
- `local_mem*`, `lsu_mem_adapter`, `mmu*` (see [`virtual_memory_subsystem.md`](virtual_memory_subsystem.md)).

`MemReq`/`MemRsp` ([`sim/simx/types.h`](../../sim/simx/types.h), ~L1185)
carry `shared_ptr<mem_block_t> data` + `byteen`; a LOAD response must
carry a line payload.

---

## 4. Pipeline flow

Fetch (via `Scheduler` PC + I-cache) → Decompress (RVC) → Decode →
Sequence (uop expand) → I-buffer → Scoreboard issue gate → Operands /
`OpcUnit` register read → Dispatcher → FuncUnit lanes (ALU / FPU / LSU /
SFU{WCTL,CSR,TEX,RASTER,DXA,OM} / TCU) → commit arbiters → `OpcUnit`
writeback. Memory: LSU → coalescer → L1 `Cache` → L2/L3 `cache_cluster` →
`Memory`. Standalone, `main.cpp` loads an image into `RAM`, programs the
KMU via DCR writes, and ticks `SimPlatform` until `!any_running()`.

---

## 5. SST integration

SST mode is a compile-time opt-in where SST is the clock driver.
[`sst/vortex_gpgpu.{cpp,h}`](../../sim/simx/sst/vortex_gpgpu.cpp) is a
`SST::Component` that owns a `VortexSimulator`
([`sst/vortex_simulator.{cpp,h}`](../../sim/simx/sst/vortex_simulator.cpp),
a v3 `Processor` + `RAM`) and calls `sim_->cycle()` per SST clock tick.

The memory boundary is a **one-way timing mirror**, not a polymorphic
peer: `Memory::set_pre_send_hook` mirrors every accepted `MemReq` to SST's
`memHierarchy` as a block-aligned, byteen-masked `StandardMem::Read/Write`.
SST responses are acknowledged and discarded; the local `RAM` remains the
single source of truth for data. This satisfies the "one boundary, single
source of truth" constraint by a hook rather than the originally proposed
`MemorySST` subclass.

---

## 6. Proposed but not yet implemented

1. **Documentation lock-in** (`simx_v3_proposal` Phase 6): a promoted
   `docs/simx_architecture.md` reference, a `simx_extension_guide.md` with
   a worked "add a FuncUnit" example, and an optional CI lint rejecting
   new cross-module method calls — none exist yet (this design doc is a
   first step).
2. **SST data-routed memory peer** (`sst_simx_v3_proposal`): the full
   `MemorySST` with an `outstanding_` tag→sink map that completes `MemRsp`
   from SST's response is not built — today SST is a one-way mirror. If
   SST-driven memory *timing* should feed back into SimX, this is the
   unbuilt piece (with its leak/timeout, tag-routing, and clock-starvation
   risks).
3. **SST CI/apptainer breadth**: a host-CPU-driven SST integration
   (`ci/sst_run_app.py`), the `sst` apptainer matrix entry, and DXA/KMU-
   under-SST verification are deferred (per-test SST scripts were
   consolidated into one hostless runner).
4. **Memory-model headroom** the design deliberately left open: cache
   coherency (MESI/MOESI) is now an additive change since lines carry
   data + dirty state, and a "sleep-until-input" optimization for the
   per-cycle O(N_objects) tick is noted for future scaling.

**Superseded directions** (recorded to avoid revival): the central
`Emulator` god-object and `MemBackend`/`core->mem_read` data path (deleted
— semantics now live on the units, data lives in the hierarchy); a public
`execute()` on every FuncUnit (reverted to private); an `isa::` namespace
and SystemC (never adopted); and the `MemorySST` polymorphic-subclass SST
boundary (replaced by the `set_pre_send_hook` mirror).

---

> **Upstream divergence note.** The upstream `vortexgpgpu/vortex` PR #298
> SST integration is **intentionally absent** on this `simx_v3` line — the
> SST boundary here is the `set_pre_send_hook` mirror described in §5, not
> the upstream SST path. Future SST users should not expect the upstream
> PR #298 wiring.

---

## 7. Source proposals

This design consolidates and supersedes `simx_v3_proposal.md` and
`sst_simx_v3_proposal.md` (now removed from `docs/proposals/`). The
framework reference is [`docs/simobject.md`](../simobject.md).

1	# Build Configuration System — Design
2	
3	**Scope:** the TOML-driven build-configuration system — how a single
4	source of config values flows to RTL, simulators, runtime, and kernels;
5	the `VX_CFG_*` macro namespace; and the hardware/software layering between
6	[`VX_config.toml`](../../VX_config.toml) and
7	[`VX_types.toml`](../../VX_types.toml).
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Sources and generator
12	
13	Two TOML files are the single source of truth:
14	
15	- [`VX_config.toml`](../../VX_config.toml) — **hardware build config**
16	  (~245 keys: platform, ISA, pipeline, memory, caches, FPU, TCU, graphics,
17	  toolchain, debug). Keys carry their namespace prefix in the TOML itself
18	  (`VX_CFG_*`, `VX_DBG_*`; `[toolchain]` predicates stay bare).
19	- [`VX_types.toml`](../../VX_types.toml) — the **software-facing ISA/ABI
20	  contract** (`VX_CSR_*`, `VX_DCR_*`, `VX_ISA_*`), plus the relocated
21	  `[memmap]` (`VX_MEM_*`) and `[vm]` (`VX_VM_*`) sections and the
22	  `[[builtin]] XLEN`.
23	
24	The generator is [`ci/gen_config.py`](../../ci/gen_config.py): given one
25	`--config <toml>` and a `--format {cflags,cpp,verilog}`, it resolves the
26	symbol table from that one file (`expr:` keys are evaluated; `[[builtin]]`
27	vars come from the environment) and emits the corresponding header.
28	[`configure`](../../configure) drives this: for each `*.toml` it emits
29	`<build>/hw/<name>.vh` (Verilog `` `define ``) and `<build>/sw/<name>.h`
30	(C `#define`); `VX_types` is generated `--resolved`, and `export XLEN`
31	feeds the `[[builtin]]`.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Value flow and layering
36	
37	```
38	  VX_config.toml ──gen_config.py──► build/hw/VX_config.vh  (`define)  ──► RTL (`VX_CFG_*)
39	                                 └─► build/sw/VX_config.h   (#define)  ──► sim/runtime
40	                   gen_config.py --cflags ──► -DVX_CFG_*  ──► sim & kernel/test builds
41	
42	  VX_types.toml  ──gen_config.py──► build/hw/VX_types.vh   ──► RTL (`VX_MEM_*, `VX_CSR_*)
43	                                 └─► build/sw/VX_types.h    ──► SW/runtime (ABI contract)
44	```
45	
46	RTL includes both generated headers via
47	[`hw/rtl/VX_define.vh`](../../hw/rtl/VX_define.vh) and references
48	`` `VX_CFG_* `` / `` `VX_MEM_* `` macros directly — there is **no**
49	SystemVerilog config package.
50	
51	**Hardware/software layering.** `VX_config.toml` → `VX_config.{h,vh}` is
52	HW/sim-private. `VX_types.toml` → `VX_types.{h,vh}` is the shared ABI
53	(`VX_types.vh` consumed by RTL, `VX_types.h` by SW). The genuine HW↔SW
54	contracts — the device memory map and the VM page-table format — were
55	relocated out of `VX_config.toml` into `VX_types.toml`'s `[memmap]`/`[vm]`
56	sections (re-prefixed `VX_MEM_*` / `VX_VM_*`), so the public runtime
57	headers never include `VX_config.h`. Two CI guards enforce the boundary:
58	[`ci/check_config_boundary.sh`](../../ci/check_config_boundary.sh) and
59	`ci/check_sw_sim_boundary.sh`.
60	
61	---
62	
63	## 3. The `VX_CFG_*` namespace
64	
65	The macro namespace is authored directly in the TOML key spelling (the
66	generator has no naming logic): `VX_CFG_*` for hardware config, `VX_DBG_*`
67	for debug knobs, `VX_MEM_*`/`VX_VM_*` for the relocated contract,
68	`VX_CSR_*`/`VX_DCR_*`/`VX_ISA_*` for types, and bare `[toolchain]`
69	predicates (`ASIC`, `SYNTHESIS`, `VIVADO`, …). The public runtime header
70	[`vortex2.h`](../../sw/runtime/include/vortex2.h) is fully decoupled — it
71	uses inlined literal bit positions (e.g. `VX_ISA_EXT_*` as
72	`(1ull << (32 + N))`) rather than including any generated config. `XLEN`
73	reaches kernels/tests via `-DVX_CFG_XLEN=$(XLEN)`.
74	
75	### 3.1 Auto-generated `_ENABLED` mirrors
76	
77	Every boolean `VX_CFG_X_ENABLE` knob automatically gets an integer companion
78	`VX_CFG_X_ENABLED` (`1`/`0`), emitted by `gen_config.py` in all three outputs
79	(cflags, resolved header, unresolved header). The two forms serve different
80	consumers: `_ENABLE` is the `` `ifdef ``/`#ifdef` presence gate, `_ENABLED` is
81	the value used in arithmetic/`localparam`/C++ `if` (e.g. the `VX_CFG_MISA_*`
82	bit-packing). **Do not hand-author `_ENABLED` entries in the TOML** — author
83	only the `_ENABLE` boolean; the mirror is generated, and the resolver also
84	auto-derives it so `expr:` keys may reference `$VX_CFG_X_ENABLED` freely. This
85	makes the two forms impossible to drift and keeps a feature's on/off truth in a
86	single boolean.
87	
88	### 3.2 Derived/internal macros are **not** `VX_CFG_*`
89	
90	`VX_CFG_*` is reserved for **configuration knobs** — things a user can set via
91	`CONFIGS="-D…"`. A macro that is purely *derived* from other knobs (you would
92	never set it directly) must **not** carry the `VX_CFG_` prefix:
93	
94	- **Internal flags consumed by RTL (and/or C++)** are derived as **bare names**
95	  in [`hw/rtl/VX_define.vh`](../../hw/rtl/VX_define.vh) (and a matching C++
96	  header when a simulator also gates on them). Examples: `TCU_META_ENABLE`
97	  (= `MX or SPARSE`, mirrored in `sim/simx/tcu/tcu_unit.h`), and

# Build Configuration System — Design

**Scope:** the TOML-driven build-configuration system — how a single
source of config values flows to RTL, simulators, runtime, and kernels;
the `VX_CFG_*` macro namespace; and the hardware/software layering between
[`VX_config.toml`](../../VX_config.toml) and
[`VX_types.toml`](../../VX_types.toml).

---

## 1. Sources and generator

Two TOML files are the single source of truth:

- [`VX_config.toml`](../../VX_config.toml) — **hardware build config**
  (~245 keys: platform, ISA, pipeline, memory, caches, FPU, TCU, graphics,
  toolchain, debug). Keys carry their namespace prefix in the TOML itself
  (`VX_CFG_*`, `VX_DBG_*`; `[toolchain]` predicates stay bare).
- [`VX_types.toml`](../../VX_types.toml) — the **software-facing ISA/ABI
  contract** (`VX_CSR_*`, `VX_DCR_*`, `VX_ISA_*`), plus the relocated
  `[memmap]` (`VX_MEM_*`) and `[vm]` (`VX_VM_*`) sections and the
  `[[builtin]] XLEN`.

The generator is [`ci/gen_config.py`](../../ci/gen_config.py): given one
`--config <toml>` and a `--format {cflags,cpp,verilog}`, it resolves the
symbol table from that one file (`expr:` keys are evaluated; `[[builtin]]`
vars come from the environment) and emits the corresponding header.
[`configure`](../../configure) drives this: for each `*.toml` it emits
`<build>/hw/<name>.vh` (Verilog `` `define ``) and `<build>/sw/<name>.h`
(C `#define`); `VX_types` is generated `--resolved`, and `export XLEN`
feeds the `[[builtin]]`.

---

## 2. Value flow and layering

```
  VX_config.toml ──gen_config.py──► build/hw/VX_config.vh  (`define)  ──► RTL (`VX_CFG_*)
                                 └─► build/sw/VX_config.h   (#define)  ──► sim/runtime
                   gen_config.py --cflags ──► -DVX_CFG_*  ──► sim & kernel/test builds

  VX_types.toml  ──gen_config.py──► build/hw/VX_types.vh   ──► RTL (`VX_MEM_*, `VX_CSR_*)
                                 └─► build/sw/VX_types.h    ──► SW/runtime (ABI contract)
```

RTL includes both generated headers via
[`hw/rtl/VX_define.vh`](../../hw/rtl/VX_define.vh) and references
`` `VX_CFG_* `` / `` `VX_MEM_* `` macros directly — there is **no**
SystemVerilog config package.

**Hardware/software layering.** `VX_config.toml` → `VX_config.{h,vh}` is
HW/sim-private. `VX_types.toml` → `VX_types.{h,vh}` is the shared ABI
(`VX_types.vh` consumed by RTL, `VX_types.h` by SW). The genuine HW↔SW
contracts — the device memory map and the VM page-table format — were
relocated out of `VX_config.toml` into `VX_types.toml`'s `[memmap]`/`[vm]`
sections (re-prefixed `VX_MEM_*` / `VX_VM_*`), so the public runtime
headers never include `VX_config.h`. Two CI guards enforce the boundary:
[`ci/check_config_boundary.sh`](../../ci/check_config_boundary.sh) and
`ci/check_sw_sim_boundary.sh`.

---

## 3. The `VX_CFG_*` namespace

The macro namespace is authored directly in the TOML key spelling (the
generator has no naming logic): `VX_CFG_*` for hardware config, `VX_DBG_*`
for debug knobs, `VX_MEM_*`/`VX_VM_*` for the relocated contract,
`VX_CSR_*`/`VX_DCR_*`/`VX_ISA_*` for types, and bare `[toolchain]`
predicates (`ASIC`, `SYNTHESIS`, `VIVADO`, …). The public runtime header
[`vortex2.h`](../../sw/runtime/include/vortex2.h) is fully decoupled — it
uses inlined literal bit positions (e.g. `VX_ISA_EXT_*` as
`(1ull << (32 + N))`) rather than including any generated config. `XLEN`
reaches kernels/tests via `-DVX_CFG_XLEN=$(XLEN)`.

### 3.1 Auto-generated `_ENABLED` mirrors

Every boolean `VX_CFG_X_ENABLE` knob automatically gets an integer companion
`VX_CFG_X_ENABLED` (`1`/`0`), emitted by `gen_config.py` in all three outputs
(cflags, resolved header, unresolved header). The two forms serve different
consumers: `_ENABLE` is the `` `ifdef ``/`#ifdef` presence gate, `_ENABLED` is
the value used in arithmetic/`localparam`/C++ `if` (e.g. the `VX_CFG_MISA_*`
bit-packing). **Do not hand-author `_ENABLED` entries in the TOML** — author
only the `_ENABLE` boolean; the mirror is generated, and the resolver also
auto-derives it so `expr:` keys may reference `$VX_CFG_X_ENABLED` freely. This
makes the two forms impossible to drift and keeps a feature's on/off truth in a
single boolean.

### 3.2 Derived/internal macros are **not** `VX_CFG_*`

`VX_CFG_*` is reserved for **configuration knobs** — things a user can set via
`CONFIGS="-D…"`. A macro that is purely *derived* from other knobs (you would
never set it directly) must **not** carry the `VX_CFG_` prefix:

- **Internal flags consumed by RTL (and/or C++)** are derived as **bare names**
  in [`hw/rtl/VX_define.vh`](../../hw/rtl/VX_define.vh) (and a matching C++
  header when a simulator also gates on them). Examples: `TCU_META_ENABLE`
  (= `MX or SPARSE`, mirrored in `sim/simx/tcu/tcu_unit.h`), and
  `IMUL_DPI`/`IDIV_DPI` (sim-only DPI integer mul/div = `not SYNTHESIS and SV_DPI`).
- **TOML-internal-only helpers** — consumed *only* by other `expr:` keys, never
  by RTL/C++ — are **lowercase private locals**, which `gen_config.py` never
  emits. Examples: `dpi_is_enabled` (= `$SV_DPI`),
  `fpu_dsp_quartus`/`fpu_dsp_vivado`.

This keeps `VX_CFG_*` an honest catalog of what is actually configurable, rather
than a mix of knobs and computed results.

---

## 4. Proposed but not yet implemented

1. **SystemVerilog typed-config package** (`config_macro_namespace` §9,
   `config_hw_sw_layering` §2.2) — **deliberately not done and not to be
   re-attempted without first solving sv2v re-export.** A typed-localparam
   `VX_config_pkg`/`VX_types_pkg` was built and reverted: sv2v drops
   wildcard `export pkg::*` symbols (the yosys ASIC flow failed on
   `L3_CACHE_SIZE` etc.), and package compile-ordering is tool-divergent
   (Verilator strict, Vivado auto-sorts, VCS order-sensitive). Backtick
   macros are the one representation every tool handles identically. The
   post-mortem rationale is the load-bearing artifact to preserve.
2. **RTL VM Sv39** — `VX_VM_ADDR_MODE` resolves to `SV39` for XLEN=64 in
   `VX_types.toml`, but `VX_mmu_ptw.sv` is hardcoded Sv32 (see
   [`virtual_memory_subsystem.md`](virtual_memory_subsystem.md) §8).
3. **MISA caps-backend leak** — `sw/runtime/{rtlsim,simx,gem5}/vortex.cpp`
   fabricate `VX_CAPS_ISA_FLAGS` from `VX_CFG_MISA_*` rather than reading
   the device model; deferred to the capability-register consolidation
   (now landed; see [`command_processor.md`](command_processor.md)
   §6). `vortex2.h` still carries "match VX_CFG_MISA_EXT" drift-hazard
   comments.

**Superseded directions** (recorded to avoid revival): `ci/check_public_headers.sh`
(replaced by `check_config_boundary.sh`); the
`VX_gpu_pkg import VX_types_pkg` package-import model (RTL reads
`VX_types.vh` backtick macros directly); and the `[isa_signatures]`
expansion (dissolved to `VX_CFG_MISA_STD/EXT` with literal bit shifts).
Note: both source proposals still carry "Draft"/"not approved" status
headers despite their cores being landed.

---

## 5. Source proposals

This design consolidates and supersedes `config_hw_sw_layering_proposal.md`
and `config_macro_namespace_proposal.md` (now removed from
`docs/proposals/`).

# Kernel Entry & Multi-Entry `.vxbin` — Design

**Scope:** how a Vortex kernel binary is entered — the unified CTA
prologue, the `.weak kernel_main` model, and the multi-entry `.vxbin`
symbol-table mechanism that lets one binary hold several named kernels
(the device-side foundation for PoCL / multi-kernel programs). Covers
[`sw/kernel/src/vx_start.S`](../../sw/kernel/src/vx_start.S),
[`sw/kernel/scripts/vxbin.py`](../../sw/kernel/scripts/vxbin.py),
the link scripts, and
[`sw/runtime/common/module.cpp`](../../sw/runtime/common/module.cpp).

---

## 1. Unified entry model

There is a single shared CTA prologue `__vx_cta_entry`
([`vx_start.S:69-136`](../../sw/kernel/src/vx_start.S#L69)) that sets up
SATP/gp/sp/tp+TLS, runs `__libc_init_array`, loads kargs into `a0` from
`MSCRATCH`, and dispatches with `jalr ra, s11` (`s11`, callee-saved,
carries the kernel/trampoline address). `_start` is itself a 2-instruction
stub ([`:30-66`](../../sw/kernel/src/vx_start.S#L30)):
`lla s11, kernel_main; j __vx_cta_entry`, with `kernel_main` declared
`.weak` so a multi-entry program needs no dead default stub (the
PC-relative `lla` resolves a weak-undef to 0 cleanly). Per-kernel entry
stubs live in a `.vx_entry` section, `KEEP`'d against `--gc-sections` by
both link scripts ([`link32.ld:59-61`](../../sw/kernel/scripts/link32.ld#L59),
`link64.ld:59-61`). The dispatch `jalr` is emitted under `.option norvc`
so it stays 4 bytes for CTA rewind.

---

## 2. Multi-entry `.vxbin` format

[`vxbin.py`](../../sw/kernel/scripts/vxbin.py) scans the linked ELF for
`__vx_kentry_*` symbols and, if any exist, appends a `VXSYMTAB` footer
([`:69-104`](../../sw/kernel/scripts/vxbin.py#L69)): a string blob + packed
`(name → PC)` entries + count + magic. A binary with no such symbols is
**byte-identical** to the legacy single-entry format.

The on-disk `.vxbin` layout is `[min_vma][max_vma][image][VXSYMTAB?]`. The
runtime loader [`module.cpp:75-119`](../../sw/runtime/common/module.cpp#L75)
sniffs the trailing magic: with a footer it parses the entries and
`vx_module_get_kernel(name)` resolves a name to a PC; without a footer it
synthesizes a single `"main"` → `min_vma` entry. This keeps legacy
single-kernel binaries working unchanged.

---

## 3. Flow

1. The compiler emits one `__vx_kentry_<name>` stub per kernel into
   `.vx_entry`; `vxbin.py` records them in the `VXSYMTAB` footer.
2. At load, `vx_module_load_file/bytes` parses the footer into a
   name→PC table.
3. `vx_module_get_kernel("<name>")` returns a `vx_kernel_h`; launch
   programs that PC into the KMU.
4. Every kernel shares `__vx_cta_entry`; `s11` carries its entry address,
   kargs arrive in `a0`.

[`tests/regression/multikernel/`](../../tests/regression/multikernel/)
(`kentry.S` with `add_k`/`mul_k`/`acc_k`) is the POCL-free in-tree test of
the multi-entry path.

---

## 4. Proposed but not yet implemented

1. **Single-entry regression re-validation** (proposal §8): the ~50
   single-entry `tests/regression` kernels should be re-run to confirm the
   legacy path's move from a direct `jal kernel_main` to `jalr ra, s11`
   (PoCL's runs already prove `jalr`/CTA-rewind compatibility; this is a
   test-coverage TODO, not a code gap).
2. **PoCL trampoline interop** (`__vx_tramp_<name>`) lives in the external
   mesa/PoCL tree; `__vx_cta_entry` is agnostic to it by design.

---

## 5. Source proposal

This design consolidates and supersedes `kmu_kernel_entry_proposal.md`
(now removed from `docs/proposals/`). The runtime module/kernel handle API
is in [`vortex_runtime_api.md`](vortex_runtime_api.md); the KMU CTA
dispatch is in [`cta_clustering_and_dispatch.md`](cta_clustering_and_dispatch.md).

# SimObject Framework

The `simobject.h` framework is the core simulation runtime used by the SimX
cycle-accurate simulator. It provides three primitives:

- **`SimObject<Impl>`** — a CRTP base for cycle-tickable simulation modules.
- **`SimChannel<Pkt>`** — a typed transport between modules with delay-based
  delivery, optional capacity backpressure, and bind-time type conversion.
- **`SimPlatform`** — a singleton that owns objects, drives the global tick
  loop, and runs an event-driven scheduler (timing wheel + delta cycles).

A working SimX module is a class derived from `SimObject<Self>` that owns
its `SimChannel`s as members and implements `on_tick()` / `on_reset()`.

---

## The Cardinal Rule

**Modules communicate *only* through channels.**

A `SimObject` may observe or mutate another module's state *only* through its
bound `SimChannel` ports — `MemReq`/`MemRsp`, `result_if`, and the like. It must
**never reach across the ownership hierarchy** to touch another object directly:

```cpp
// WRONG — a leaf unit climbs Core -> Processor to grab the global Memory
// and read/write its DRAM backing store, bypassing the modeled cache path.
auto* gmem = core_->processor()->memsim();
gmem->write_bytes(&e.data, e.addr, e.size);

// RIGHT — the unit drives its own output channel; the request flows through
// the coalescer/cache/NoC just as the wires do in RTL.
out_req.try_send(MemReq{ .addr = e.addr, .op = MemOp::STORE, ... });
```

Why this is non-negotiable:

- **Channels *are* the wires.** The `SimChannel` graph is the SimX model of the
  chip's actual connectivity. A module's only path to the rest of the system is
  the set of ports it was wired to. Reaching around them models hardware that
  doesn't exist.
- **It preserves timing/functional fidelity and SimX↔RTL parity.** A unit that
  side-doors the backing store can read a value that, on real silicon, is still
  in flight through the cache hierarchy — producing SimX-only results the RTL
  never yields. Going through the channel path keeps the timing model and the
  functional effect consistent, which is what makes SimX a faithful oracle for RTL.
- **Hierarchy is ownership, not a call graph.** `Core` *owns* its units and
  `Processor` *owns* the `Memory`; that parent→child ownership exists for
  lifetime/construction, and must not be walked upward (`child->parent()->…`)
  or laterally to invoke a sibling's internals.

input.rationale: Vortex 是一个全栈开源 RISC-V GPGPU（主机运行时→驱动后端→SimX 仿真器→RTL→FPGA），体量大、子系统多，因此按"先认清全栈与运行方式，再沿软件栈下行到模拟器/RTL/内存，最后深入加速器、图形、虚拟内存、上层 API 与工程化"的顺序组织成 14 个单元、约 46 篇讲义。入门层（U1）让读者从零跑通 demo 并建立全栈心智模型；进阶层（U2–U8）沿"配置系统→主机运行时/驱动→设备内核 API→SimX 框架→核心流水线(SimX)→核心流水线(RTL)→内存/缓存"这条自顶向下的主链路展开，强调 SimX 与 RTL 的模型一致性这条贯穿主线；专家层（U9–U14）覆盖张量核/DXA、图形/光追、虚拟内存/原子/命令处理器、OpenCL/Vulkan/HIP 上层栈，以及测试调试、性能、FPGA/综合与二次开发。每篇讲义只解决一个主题、绑定真实源码与一个可操作的实践任务，并通过 depends_on 形成清晰的可学习 DAG。

units.title: 入门：项目总览与首次运行

lectures.title: Vortex 是什么：全栈开源 RISC-V GPGPU
lectures.topic: 介绍 Vortex 的定位、全栈构成（sim/RTL/FPGA 多后端驱动）、SIMT 执行模型与 RISC-V ISA 扩展（TMC/WSPAWN/SPLIT/JOIN/BAR）。
learning_goals: 理解 Vortex 全栈从主机运行时到 FPGA 的分层构成
掌握 SIMT 下的 thread/warp/socket/cluster 层次模型
了解 Vortex 对 RISC-V 做了哪些类 GPU 的 ISA 扩展
minimal_modules: Microarchitecture 执行模型与 ISA 扩展
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 README 与 microarchitecture 文档，画一张『主机→驱动后端→模拟器/RTL/FPGA』的全栈分层图，并标注每一层对应的仓库目录（sw/runtime、sim、hw、ci）。

理解 tests 下不同测试套件的定位

lectures.topic: 讲解 out-of-tree 构建、configure 脚本如何生成可运行树、toolchain 安装，以及『改了 toml/Makefile 必须重新 configure』这条核心规则。

lectures.title: TOML 配置：唯一的真相来源
lectures.topic: 讲解 VX_config.toml（硬件构建配置）与 VX_types.toml（软件 ABI 契约）两个真相来源，以及 VX_CFG_*/VX_MEM_*/VX_CSR_* 宏命名空间。
learning_goals: 区分 VX_config.toml 与 VX_types.toml 的职责

lectures.title: 核心流水线各级 RTL

data.head: d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d
data.rationale: Vortex 是一个全栈开源 RISC-V GPGPU（主机运行时→驱动后端→SimX 仿真器→RTL→FPGA），体量大、子系统多，因此按"先认清全栈与运行方式，再沿软件栈下行到模拟器/RTL/内存，最后深入加速器、图形、虚拟内存、上层 API 与工程化"的顺序组织成 14 个单元、约 46 篇讲义。入门层（U1）让读者从零跑通 demo 并建立全栈心智模型；进阶层（U2–U8）沿"配置系统→主机运行时/驱动→设备内核 API→SimX 框架→核心流水线(SimX)→核心流水线(RTL)→内存/缓存"这条自顶向下的主链路展开，强调 SimX 与 RTL 的模型一致性这条贯穿主线；专家层（U9–U14）覆盖张量核/DXA、图形/光追、虚拟内存/原子/命令处理器、OpenCL/Vulkan/HIP 上层栈，以及测试调试、性能、FPGA/综合与二次开发。每篇讲义只解决一个主题、绑定真实源码与一个可操作的实践任务，并通过 depends_on 形成清晰的可学习 DAG。

units.title: 入门：项目总览与首次运行

lectures.title: Vortex 是什么：全栈开源 RISC-V GPGPU
lectures.topic: 介绍 Vortex 的定位、全栈构成（sim/RTL/FPGA 多后端驱动）、SIMT 执行模型与 RISC-V ISA 扩展（TMC/WSPAWN/SPLIT/JOIN/BAR）。
learning_goals: 理解 Vortex 全栈从主机运行时到 FPGA 的分层构成
掌握 SIMT 下的 thread/warp/socket/cluster 层次模型
了解 Vortex 对 RISC-V 做了哪些类 GPU 的 ISA 扩展
minimal_modules: Microarchitecture 执行模型与 ISA 扩展
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 README 与 microarchitecture 文档，画一张『主机→驱动后端→模拟器/RTL/FPGA』的全栈分层图，并标注每一层对应的仓库目录（sw/runtime、sim、hw、ci）。

learning_goals: 记住仓库一级目录与各自职责

lectures.title: 构建系统、configure 与工具链
lectures.topic: 讲解 out-of-tree 构建、configure 脚本如何生成可运行树、toolchain 安装，以及『改了 toml/Makefile 必须重新 configure』这条核心规则。
learning_goals: 掌握 build 目录与 configure 的关系
理解 configure 如何生成 config.mk/common.mk 并嵌入工具路径
知道为何 VX_config.toml 改动后必须重新 configure

lectures.practice_task: 在 build 目录执行 ../configure --xlen=64，打开生成的 config.mk 与某 domain common.mk，找到 Verilator/RISC-V 工具的绝对路径，并解释为何多棵 Vortex 树可以共存。

lectures.title: 首次运行：用 blackbox.sh 跑通 demo
lectures.topic: 用 ci/blackbox.sh 作为统一启动器，以 demo 为例跑通 SimX，并介绍 --cores/--warps/--threads/--driver 等常用旋钮。
learning_goals: 能够用 blackbox.sh 在 SimX 上跑通一个程序
理解 --driver 与架构覆盖参数的含义
认识 CONFIGS=-DVX_CFG_* 与架构宏的关系
lectures.practice_task: 运行 ./ci/blackbox.sh --driver=simx --app=demo，再用 --cores=2 --warps=4 --threads=4 改变配置重跑，记录程序退出码与输出变化。

lectures.title: TOML 配置：唯一的真相来源
lectures.topic: 讲解 VX_config.toml（硬件构建配置）与 VX_types.toml（软件 ABI 契约）两个真相来源，以及 VX_CFG_*/VX_MEM_*/VX_CSR_* 宏命名空间。
learning_goals: 区分 VX_config.toml 与 VX_types.toml 的职责
理解 VX_CFG_* 宏命名空间的含义
掌握 _ENABLE 与自动生成的 _ENABLED 镜像关系

lectures.title: gen_config.py 与配置值流
lectures.topic: 讲解 ci/gen_config.py 如何把一个 toml 解析为 cflags/cpp/verilog 三种输出，configure 如何驱动它生成 .h/.vh。
learning_goals: 掌握 gen_config.py 的三种输出格式
理解配置值如何流到 RTL/sim/runtime/kernel
知道 expr: 表达式与 [[builtin]] 变量的解析
lectures.practice_task: 手动运行 gen_config.py 对 VX_config.toml 生成 cflags、cpp、verilog 三种输出并 diff，观察同一参数在三种格式下的不同表示。

lectures.title: 硬件/软件分层与边界检查
lectures.topic: 讲解 VX_config(HW/sim 私有) 与 VX_types(共享 ABI) 的分层，以及两个 CI 边界检查脚本如何强制 sw/kernel 与 hw/sim 双向隔离。
learning_goals: 理解为何公共运行时头文件不能 include VX_config.h
掌握 sw/{kernel,runtime} 与 hw/sim 的双向隔离规则
会使用 check_config_boundary.sh / check_sw_sim_boundary.sh
minimal_modules: 两个 boundary 检查脚本
lectures.practice_task: 运行两个 boundary 检查脚本，然后在 sw/kernel 下故意 #include 一个 hw/ 头文件，观察 check_sw_sim_boundary.sh 如何报错。

units.title: 软件栈：主机运行时与驱动

lectures.title: 运行时公开 API
lectures.topic: 讲解 sw/runtime/include/vortex.h 暴露的设备/缓冲区/内核启动 API，对齐 CUDA/OpenCL 风格的主机接口。
learning_goals: 掌握 vx_dev_open/close、vx_mem_alloc、vx_start、vx_ready_wait 的用法
理解 vx_upload_kernel_file 与 vx_mpm_query 的作用
能读懂一份典型主机程序的控制流
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 vortex.h，用伪代码写出『打开设备→分配缓冲→拷入数据→上传内核→启动→等待→拷回结果→关闭』的完整主机调用序列。

lectures.title: 设备、缓冲区与内存管理
lectures.topic: 深入 runtime/common 的 device.cpp/buffer.cpp/vm.cpp，理解设备句柄、缓冲区对象与设备虚拟内存管理的关系。
learning_goals: 理解 device 与 buffer 对象的内部结构
掌握 vx_copy_to_dev/vx_copy_from_dev 的数据通路
了解设备侧地址空间与 vm 的关系
lectures.practice_task: 跟踪 vx_mem_alloc 到底层，画出 device↔buffer↔vm 的对象关系图，并标注一次 copy_to_dev 经过哪些对象。

lectures.title: 驱动后端与 stub 动态分发
lectures.topic: 讲解 libvortex.so 的 stub 分发机制：首次 vx_dev_open 时按 $VORTEX_DRIVER dlopen 后端库（simx/rtlsim/opae/xrt/gem5）。
learning_goals: 理解 stub/vortex.cpp 如何用 dlopen 选择后端
掌握 callbacks_t 分发表与 dispatcher.h 的契约
认识五种驱动后端的定位差异
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 stub/vortex.cpp，解释 VORTEX_DRIVER 环境变量如何决定加载哪个 .so，并列出 simx 后端需要实现的关键回调。

lectures.title: 主机→设备启动流程与 .vxbin 加载
lectures.topic: 讲解 module.cpp 如何解析 .vxbin 的 VXSYMTAB 多入口符号表，以及 vx_start 如何把 kernel+arguments 程序进 KMU。
learning_goals: 理解 .vxbin 单入口与多入口格式的兼容设计
掌握 vx_module_get_kernel 的名字→PC 解析
了解 vx_start 到命令处理器/KMU 的衔接
lectures.practice_task: 跟踪 vx_upload_kernel_file → vx_start 的调用链，画出从主机加载 .vxbin 到 KMU 收到启动 PC 的完整数据流。

lectures.title: 内核运行时启动与入口模型
lectures.topic: 讲解 sw/kernel/src/vx_start.S 的统一 CTA prologue __vx_cta_entry，以及 vxbin.py 的多入口符号表机制。
learning_goals: 理解 __vx_cta_entry 如何设置 SATP/gp/sp/tp 并用 s11 派发
掌握 kernel_main 的 .weak 模型与 .vx_entry 段
了解 VXSYMTAB footer 的磁盘布局
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 vx_start.S 的 __vx_cta_entry，写出它依次做了哪些寄存器/段设置，并解释为何 dispatch 的 jalr 要 .option norvc。

lectures.title: SIMT 控制指令与 warp 调度 API
lectures.topic: 讲解 vx_intrinsics.h 与 vx_spawn.h 暴露的 TMC/WSPAWN/SPLIT/JOIN/PRED 等 warp 控制内联函数，及其与 SIMT 模型的对应。
learning_goals: 掌握 warp 派生（WSPAWN）与线程激活（TMC）API
理解分支发散的 SPLIT/JOIN 与 IPDOM 栈
能在一个真实 kernel 中识别这些控制指令
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 tests/regression/demo 的 kernel 源码，找出 warp 派生与线程激活调用，画出 grid/block/warp 的派生关系图。

lectures.title: printf、barrier 与系统调用
lectures.topic: 讲解设备侧的 vx_printf（COUT 环）、vx_barrier 同步，以及 vx_syscalls.c 提供的轻量系统调用服务。
learning_goals: 理解 vx_printf 如何通过 COUT 环输出到主机
掌握 vx_barrier 的栅栏语义
了解内核侧 syscall 的最小实现
lectures.practice_task: 在 tests/regression/printf 中增加一个 vx_printf 调用，在 SimX 上运行并观察输出，解释 CoutDrainer 如何在 main.cpp 中排空 COUT 环。

lectures.title: SimObject/SimChannel/SimPlatform 基元
lectures.topic: 讲解 simobject.h 的三大基元：CRTP 的 SimObject、带延迟与背压的 SimChannel、以及驱动 tick 的 SimPlatform 时序轮。
learning_goals: 掌握 SimObject 的 on_tick/on_reset 钩子
理解 SimChannel 的 send/delay 与容量背压
了解 SimPlatform 的 timing wheel + delta 事件
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 simobject.h 与 simobject.md，用一段话解释『channel 就是流水线』的含义，并说明一个流水线单元为何不需要内部 stage deque。

lectures.title: SimX 入口与处理器层次
lectures.topic: 讲解 main.cpp 的独立 CLI 驱动，以及 processor→cluster→socket→core 的 GPU 实例化层次。
learning_goals: 掌握 main.cpp 的启动流程（建 RAM、attach、写 DCR、load image、tick）
理解 Processor 如何持有 clusters 与单一 Memory
了解 core→socket→cluster 的层次关系
lectures.practice_task: 跟踪 main.cpp 的启动序列，列出 KMU 启动相关的 DCR 写入（STARTUP_ADDR、GRID/BLOCK_DIM 等），并解释 any_running() 何时为假。

lectures.title: 基数规则与模块分解
lectures.topic: 讲解『模块只通过 channel 通信』的基数规则，以及 SimX v3 模块分解（语义与时序同居一处）如何成为 RTL 的预言机。
learning_goals: 理解基数规则为何不可违反
掌握 SimX 与 RTL 逐模块对应的关系
认识 MemReq/MemRsp 在 types.h 中的数据载荷定义
lectures.practice_task: 在 types.h 中找到 MemReq/MemRsp 结构，解释为何 LOAD 响应必须携带 line 数据载荷（而非通过 core->mem_read 后门）。

units.title: GPU 执行模型与核心流水线（SimX 视角）

lectures.title: Warp 调度器、CTA 派发与屏障
lectures.topic: 讲解 scheduler/cta_dispatcher/barrier_unit 如何管理 warp 生命周期、把 CTA 拆成 warp 并处理屏障。
learning_goals: 掌握 warp 的 PC/tmask/IPDOM 状态管理
理解 CTA→warp 的 block/grid 映射
了解 BAR 屏障的到达与释放
lectures.practice_task: 跟踪一个 CTA 如何被拆成多个 warp、分配 PC 与 tmask，并用 IPDOM 栈解释一次分支发散后的汇聚。

lectures.title: 取指、解压、译码与微操作展开
lectures.topic: 讲解 decode/decompressor/sequencer：RVC 解压、RISC-V 译码成 Instr、以及 sequencer 把 TCU WGMMA 展开为多微操作。
learning_goals: 掌握 RVC 压缩指令的解压流程
理解 Instr 解码结构
了解 sequencer 的微操作展开（多 uop 的 WMMA/WGMMA）
lectures.practice_task: 解释一条 RVC 压缩指令从 fetch 到 decode 的流程，并以 WGMMA 为例说明 sequencer 为何需要展开成多个微操作。

lectures.title: 发射、记分板与操作数收集
lectures.topic: 讲解 scoreboard/opc_unit/operands/dispatcher：ibuffer、寄存器冒险检测、每 warp 寄存器堆与写回。
learning_goals: 掌握 ibuffer 的按 warp 队列与发射门控
理解 scoreboard 的寄存器冒险跟踪与顺序完成
了解 OpcUnit 如何持有每 warp 寄存器堆并完成写回
lectures.practice_task: 解释 scoreboard 如何判断一条指令能否发射，并画出 operands→OpcUnit 读寄存器→dispatcher 派发到 FU 的数据通路。

lectures.title: 功能单元 ALU/FPU/LSU/SFU
lectures.topic: 讲解 FuncUnit<NUM_BLOCKS> CRTP 基类，以及 ALU/FPU/LSU/SFU 各自私有 execute() 如何承载 ISA 语义。
learning_goals: 掌握 FuncUnit CRTP 基类的 Inputs/Outputs channel 模型
理解 ALU/FPU 私有 execute 的语义归属
了解 SFU 作为分派器路由到 WCTL/CSR/TEX/RASTER/DXA/OM 子单元
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 func_unit.h，写出一个新 FuncUnit 需要实现哪些 channel 与钩子，并解释 SFU 为何是分派器而非单一执行单元。

lectures.title: Vortex 顶层与 socket/cluster RTL
lectures.topic: 讲解 Vortex.sv 顶层与 VX_socket.sv/VX_cluster.sv 的实例化层次，以及 VX_gpu_pkg.sv 的作用。
learning_goals: 掌握 Vortex 顶层模块的实例化结构
理解 socket（共享 L1）与 cluster（共享 L2）的 RTL 组织
了解 VX_gpu_pkg.sv 与 VX_define.vh 的关系
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 Vortex.sv，画出 socket→cluster→core 的实例化层次，并标注 L1/L2 缓存的共享边界。

lectures.title: 核心流水线各级 RTL
lectures.topic: 对照 SimX 的 6 级流水线，在 hw/rtl/core 中找到 fetch/decode/issue/execute/commit 各级对应模块。
learning_goals: 掌握 VX_core.sv 的流水线组织
能在 RTL 中定位 schedule/fetch/decode/issue/execute/commit
理解 RTL 与 SimX 的级间对应
lectures.practice_task: 对照 microarchitecture 的 6 级流水线，在 RTL 中逐一找到对应模块并填写一张『流水级→RTL 模块→SimX 模块』对照表。

lectures.title: 调度器与 warp 控制 RTL
lectures.topic: 讲解 VX_scheduler/VX_ibuffer/VX_scoreboard/VX_split_join/VX_ipdom_stack 如何实现 warp 调度与分支发散/汇聚。
learning_goals: 掌握 RTL 调度器与 ibuffer 的配合
理解 split/join + IPDOM 栈的发散与汇聚机制
了解 scoreboard 在 RTL 中的实现
lectures.practice_task: 解释 VX_split_join 与 VX_ipdom_stack 如何协作完成一次 divergent branch 的 SPLIT/JOIN，画出 tmask 的保存与恢复过程。

lectures.title: SimX↔RTL 模型一致性（model parity）
lectures.topic: 讲解 model_parity CI 门控：同一 app/args/configs 在 simx 与 rtlsim 上退休指令精确一致、周期误差在容差内。
learning_goals: 理解为何 SimX 必须与 RTL 保持时序/功能同步
掌握 model_parity 门控的判定标准
了解『绝不能放宽容差来吸收差异』的纪律
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 AGENTS.md §4 中关于 SimX-RTL lockstep 的规则，解释一次 RTL 流水线改动为何必须同时更新 SimX 时序模型。

units.title: 内存层次与缓存子系统

lectures.title: 内存层次与缓存子系统总览
lectures.topic: 讲解 L1/L2/L3/本地内存/DRAM 的层次与共享关系（socket 共享 L1、cluster 共享 L2），以及可选缓存配置。
learning_goals: 掌握 Vortex 的多级缓存与本地内存层次
理解 socket/cluster 与 L1/L2 的共享边界
了解缓存可选性与配置开关
lectures.practice_task: 画出 Vortex 完整内存层次图，标注 LSU→L1→L2→L3→DRAM 的路径与各级共享范围，并标出本地内存的位置。

lectures.title: 缓存标签、MSHR、替换与数据通路
lectures.topic: 深入对比 RTL 与 SimX 的 cache 实现：tags、MSHR、替换策略与数据通路。
learning_goals: 掌握 VX_cache.sv 的内部模块划分
理解 MSHR 如何处理多重未命中
能对比 RTL cache 与 SimX cache 的实现
lectures.practice_task: 对比 RTL 与 SimX 的 cache，解释 MSHR 在两个实现中如何承载未命中请求与 line 数据，并说明替换策略模块的职责。

lectures.title: 访存合并、本地内存与 DRAM 模型
lectures.topic: 讲解 mem_coalescer 的访存合并、local_mem 共享内存，以及 memory.cpp 用 ramulator2 建模的 DRAM。
learning_goals: 掌握 LSU 请求如何被 coalescer 合并
理解本地内存（共享内存）的组织
了解 DRAM 模型与 line 数据的传输
lectures.practice_task: 解释一个 warp 内多个线程的 load 如何被 coalescer 合并成更少的 cache line 请求，并说明 memory.cpp 如何用 ramulator2 提供时序。

lectures.title: LSU 流水线设计
lectures.topic: 讲解 LSU 流水线：AGU 地址生成、slice 处理，以及与缓存层次的衔接。
learning_goals: 掌握 VX_lsu_unit 的流水线结构
理解 AGU 的地址生成与 packed load
了解 store/load 从 LSU 到缓存的路径
lectures.practice_task: 跟踪一次 store 从 AGU 地址生成到进入缓存层次的完整过程，并解释 packed load 的 LsuUopGen 在 SimX 中的作用。

units.title: 高级 ISA 扩展：张量核与异步拷贝

lectures.title: 张量核 WGMMA 引擎
lectures.topic: 讲解 TCU 的 WGMMA 分块矩阵乘加、2:4 结构化稀疏与 MX 缩放，及其 kernel API vx_tensor.h。
learning_goals: 掌握 WGMMA 的分块矩阵乘加语义
理解 2:4 结构化稀疏与 MX 数据类型支持
了解 tcu_unit/tcu_tbuf 的 SimX 建模
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 vx_tensor.h 与 tests/regression/sgemm_tcu_wg，解释 WGMMA 一次操作的分块形状，并说明 2:4 结构化稀疏如何减少有效计算量。

lectures.title: DXA 异步拷贝与多播
lectures.topic: 讲解 DXA 作为异步数据传输加速器（DMA），支持一份数据多播到多个集群，及其 kernel API vx_dxa.h。
learning_goals: 掌握 DXA 的异步拷贝（DMA）模型
理解多播（multicast）如何分发数据到多个 cluster
了解 dxa_unit/dxa_core 的 SimX 建模
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 tests/regression/dxa_copy_mcast 与 sgemm2_dxa_mcast，解释一次多播 DMA 如何把一份数据同时送到多个集群的本地内存。

lectures.title: 图形硬件栈（RASTER/TEX/OM）
lectures.topic: 讲解图形固定功能流水线：光栅化（raster）、纹理（tex）、输出合并（om）在 RTL 与 SimX 中的实现。
learning_goals: 掌握图形固定功能流水线的三段
理解 RASTER/TEX/OM 的职责
能在 RTL 与 SimX 中定位对应模块
lectures.practice_task: 对照图形固定功能流水线文档，在 hw/rtl 与 sim/simx 中分别找到 raster/tex/om 对应模块，并写出每段流水线的输入输出。

lectures.title: 图形软件栈与软件发射器
lectures.topic: 讲解 sw/gfx 与 sw/common/gfx_ff_model 在主机侧模拟固定功能单元的软件发射器（software emitters）机制。
learning_goals: 理解 gfx_ff_model 如何在主机侧模拟固定功能
掌握软件发射器的作用与 ABI
了解 sw/common 中 gfx 相关头文件的分层
lectures.practice_task: 解释 gfx_ff_model 如何在主机侧模拟光栅化/纹理，使得图形测试在没有完整固定功能硬件时也能运行。

lectures.title: 硬件光线追踪单元（RTU）
lectures.topic: 讲解 RTU 的 BVH 遍历、ray-box/ray-triangle 相交测试的硬件实现，及其 kernel API vx_raytrace.h。
learning_goals: 掌握 BVH 遍历的硬件流程
理解 ray-box 与 ray-triangle 相交测试
了解 rtu_walker/rtu_isect 的 SimX 建模
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 ray_tracing_unit.md，画出一条射线从发射到命中三角形的 RTU 处理流程，标注 BVH walker 与相交测试模块。

units.title: 虚拟内存、原子操作与命令处理器

lectures.title: 虚拟内存子系统
lectures.topic: 讲解 Sv32/Sv39 页表遍历、TLB，以及主机运行时如何为设备建立页表（vm.cpp / vm_types.h）。
learning_goals: 掌握 Vortex 的页表格式与 PTW
理解 TLB 的作用与 miss 处理
了解主机运行时如何为设备分配并建立页表
lectures.practice_task: 解释 Sv32 页表遍历的过程，并说明主机运行时 vm.cpp 如何把设备虚拟地址映射到物理内存（注意 RTL 当前仍硬编码 Sv32 的待确认点）。

lectures.title: 原子内存操作与多缓存一致性
lectures.topic: 讲解 AMO 的 read-modify-write 在缓存层次中的实现，以及多缓存间的 AMO 一致性保证。
learning_goals: 掌握 AMO 在缓存中的 RMW 实现
理解多缓存 AMO 一致性的仲裁
了解 amo_unit 在 SimX 与 RTL 的对应
lectures.practice_task: 用 tests/regression/amo 中的例子解释一次原子加如何在多缓存环境下保持正确性，并说明 AMO 为何要被路由到特定缓存点。

lectures.title: 命令处理器与 KMU
lectures.topic: 讲解一次 kernel launch 从主机 DCR 写入，到 CP（VX_cp_core/VX_cp_launch）解包，再到 KMU 分发 CTA 的完整路径。
learning_goals: 掌握命令处理器 CP 的 AXI-L 寄存器接口与解包
理解 KMU 如何根据 grid/block/cluster 维度派发 CTA
了解 SimX kmu.cpp 与 RTL CP 的对应
lectures.practice_task: 跟踪一次 vx_start 触发的 launch：主机写 DCR→CP 解包→KMU 派发 CTA，画出完整的控制流并标注 grid/block/cluster 维度的来源。

lectures.title: OpenCL 支持（PoCL）
lectures.topic: 讲解 Vortex 通过 PoCL 提供 OpenCL 1.2 支持，PoCL 如何把 OpenCL 程序映射到 Vortex 运行时与 VOLT 编译器。
learning_goals: 掌握 OpenCL 经 PoCL 运行在 Vortex 的路径
理解 PoCL→vortex runtime 的衔接
了解 tests/opencl 测试套件的组织
lectures.practice_task: 用 blackbox 或 tests/opencl 跑一个 OpenCL kernel（如 copybuf 或 backprop），解释 OpenCL API 调用如何最终落到 vortex.h 的运行时接口。

lectures.title: Vulkan 支持（vortexpipe / mesa）
lectures.topic: 讲解 mesa-vortex 驱动与 vortexpipe 架构如何把 Vulkan 映射到 Vortex 的图形/计算栈。
learning_goals: 掌握 Vulkan 经 mesa-vortex 运行的架构
理解 vortexpipe 的分层职责
了解图形软件栈与 Vulkan 的衔接
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 vortexpipe_architecture.md，画出 Vulkan API → mesa-vortex 驱动 → Vortex 图形/计算栈的映射路径。

lectures.title: HIP 支持（chipStar）
lectures.topic: 讲解 Vortex 通过 chipStar 提供 HIP 支持，HIP 程序如何经 SPIR-V 编译并运行在 Vortex 上。
learning_goals: 掌握 HIP 经 chipStar 运行的路径
理解 SPIR-V 在编译链中的作用
了解 tests/hip 测试套件
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 hip_on_vortex_chipstar.md，用 tests/hip 中的 sgemm/vecadd 例子解释 HIP kernel 如何被编译并在 Vortex 上执行。

lectures.title: 测试与回归流程
lectures.topic: 讲解 tests 套件组织、make run-simx/run-rtlsim 回归，以及 ci/regression.sh 与声明式 testcases 目录。
learning_goals: 掌握 tests 下各类测试套件的定位
会用 make run-simx 与 ci/regression.sh 跑回归
理解 CONFIGS 与架构宏在测试中的作用
lectures.practice_task: 运行 make -C tests/regression run-simx 跑一类回归，再用 ci/regression.sh --test <category> 选择一个测试类别并记录结果。

lectures.title: 调试追踪与 SimX-as-oracle
lectures.topic: 讲解 --debug 生成运行时 trace、trace_csv.py 解析、Perfetto 分析，以及 RTL 调试卡住时的 SimX-as-oracle 模式。
learning_goals: 会用 --debug 生成 trace 并用 trace_csv.py 解析
